column2: with loose hair and rolling eyes, deep red, her feet on a banner fluttering in the wind, her body like a lotus,
bereft of discrimination, intoxicated, beyond pride, shame and fear — contemplating her thus, one should worship the chakra with the naked Goddess in the middle.
One should worship with hibiscus, pomegranate, bandhuka, kimshuka and the like, and with other fragrant flowers such as shephali.
Within three times seven nights she comes in the form described, overcome with passion, and does not leave him as long as his body lasts.
By oblation of red lotuses smeared with the three sweets one gains prosperity; likewise with red water-lilies one brings women under one's control.
By offering mallika, malati, jati and hundred-petalled lotuses soaked in the milk of a white cow with a calf of the same colour,
one gains fame, learning, wealth, health, good fortune, riches and the like; by oblation of aragvadha flowers smeared with honey
comes gold and the like, the paralysis of enemies, and of the anger of kings and others; by oblation of red oleander flowers smeared with ghee
come red garments, women, and control over kings and ministers, and the ornaments, vehicles and success in trade that he desires.
By oblation of salt, mustard and other things smeared with oil at midnight, one brings the woman one desires.
One should offer black dara flowers smeared with oil at night; within a month the enemy surely suffers from fever.
By oblation at night of marking-nuts smeared with ghee, and their seeds, the enemy develops burning sores that physicians can hardly cure.
Likewise with ankola seeds sprinkled with that oil, and with pepper and mustard smeared with ghee, by oblation at night,
one quickly brings the desired woman, afflicted with the fever of love. With rice sprinkled with ghee, by oblation one gains rice;
with mung, mung; with ghee, ghee — so it comes about by such offerings. Making an effigy from the tree of the target's constellation, of flour and the dust of his footprints,
and of mustard, pepper and salt, one should offer it at night; from the toes, shanks, knees and thighs,
below the navel, from the heart, from the throat and the head, cutting it in order with a very sharp weapon —
by thus offering it in twelve pieces, men, women and kings come under control within seven days, or suffer fever, as he wishes.
Making an effigy of flour with jaggery, pepper and cumin, with the target's name on its heart,
and cooking it again in the ghee left from the oblation with the name, touching it with one's fingertips, one should recite the mantra a thousand times;
having worshipped it, smeared with ghee, one should eat it, thinking of the target while reciting; men, women and kings then remain under his control until death.
Grinding the eight perfumes of the Shakti with a maiden's help in cool water and wearing a tilaka of it on the forehead, one brings the world under control.
Taking a prastha of shali rice, one should put it in a new pot, with the milk of a red cow whose calf is of the same colour,
putting in twice that amount, and cook it on a consecrated fire; making a ball sprinkled with ghee, with sugar, in the hand,
reciting the vidya a hundred and eight times, one should then offer it; this oblation made on the first lunar day brings great prosperity.
Done likewise on Fridays, within a year one becomes like a king. On the fifth day especially one should perform the oblation as before;
on that day one should offer white mallika and other flowers smeared with the three sweets; offering food and ghee regularly, a man becomes rich in food.
Whatever thing one desires, all of it one always obtains by oblations of ghee, and likewise of sesame and rice.
Making oblations with red lotuses soaked in the three sweets, within a mandala of forty days one gains great and praiseworthy prosperity.
With fully blown, fine kahlara flowers sprinkled with honey one should offer a thousand daily with devotion from the full-moon day up to that day;
he gains fame, wealth and sons without doubt. By a thousand oblations of champaka flowers sprinkled with honey one surely
gains a hundred gold coins within a month, O Narada. Likewise by three thousand oblations of patala flowers sprinkled with ghee
within a month from the new moon one gains colourful garments, and within a month fragrant things like camphor and sandal,
and other pleasing things useful for enjoyment. A hundred oblations of shali rice sprinkled with milk on the seventh days
bring abundance of rice within six months without doubt. By oblations of sesame for a year one gains health.
A man who offers durva on his three birth-constellation days lives a hundred years free from fear and with great enjoyment.
Or one may offer guduchi, sesame and durva on the three birth days; thereby one becomes rich in long life, prosperity, fame, enjoyment, merit, treasure and the like.
By offering ghee, milk-rice and milk on those three in order, one becomes a king's minister with long life, health and wealth.
By an oblation of bananas on the seventh one gains good fortune daily. With triple sprigs of durva a span long joined with the three sweets
one should offer daily in a terrible fever of the three humours; on those days one should recite the vidya daily while touching water,
a thousand times, and use that water for bathing and drinking, and for cooking and the like, to be freed from the disease.
Powder of the tree of the target's constellation, the three pungents, mustard, sesame and flour, joined with the dust of the target's footprints —
making an effigy with the name on its heart, one should strike it, cutting it as before with sharp iron weapons.
Thus within seven days the target becomes firmly subject. Burying such an effigy in the middle of the fire-pit,
placing fire above it, one should daily offer with the vidya three thousand oblations of mustard soaked in its juice for three watches;
one draws a woman forcibly even from a hundred yojanas away. By oblation of kaushika mixed with honey one brings a woman under control;
with coconuts and jaggery one gains prosperity; likewise with kahlara soaked in ghee, with red lotuses smeared with milk,
with champaka smeared with the three sweets, with bakula flowers, and with madhuka flowers — by these oblations one obtains a maiden.
By oblations of punnaga flowers one gains garments; with ghee, what one desires; with buffalo ghee, buffaloes; with goat ghee, goats; with cow ghee, cows;
by oblations of ghee with gems the practitioner gains gems. Making an effigy of rice flour with sugar,
with the letters of the name placed on its heart, one should cook it in oil and ghee at night, and, thinking of the target day and night, eat it, consecrated with the vidya.
By this seven-night rite a man, a woman or even a king comes under control like a servant and would give up mind, life and all.
Likewise one should offer red or white oleander flowers; within three times seven nights a man gains great prosperity.
By oblation of goat's flesh smeared with the three sweets one gains gold; with the same smeared with milk, within a mandala one gains land rich in crops.
By oblation of lotus seeds one gains prosperity in three days; in the preparatory japa one should offer a tenth with bilva, beginning with the mantra.
The practitioner whose mantra is thus perfected can revive those dead of snakebite by striking their mouths with handfuls of consecrated water,
reciting the vidya into their ears, or striking the head suddenly with a staff perfected by japa, he raises the dead.
Making a yoni-shaped pit, one should duly offer into its fire sesame, mustard, wheat, rice, grain and barley,
smeared with the three sweets, singly or together, for prosperity; with bakula, champaka, lotuses, kahlara and red lotuses,
with water-lilies, mallika, kunda and madhuka to gain Indira; with ashoka, patala, bilva, jati and white vikankata,
with fresh blue lotuses, oleander and karnikara, by oblation one gains prosperity, good fortune, treasure, long life and fame.
Offering durva, guduchi, ashvattha, banyan, aragvadha, white arka and plaksha, one is freed from long-standing disease.
With sugarcane, jambu, coconut and banana joined with jaggery and sugar, one surely gains lasting prosperity and becomes an enjoyer of it.
Offering mustard and ghee in a fire of death-wood brings death to the enemy; by oblations of chaturangula, the fourfold army of the enemy
within seven days is surely afflicted by disease and sorrow; there is no doubt. One should always perform the daily worship and the oblation with ghee,
and drink water consecrated with the vidya in the morning to attain it. With sandal, ushira, camphor, musk and gorochana,
with saffron, black aloe-wood and deer musk — with these perfumes one should worship Shiva for success in all aims.
In the morning one should drink water consecrated three times with all the Nityas together with the alphabet, and likewise for success in speech, [worship] Shiva.
One should perform the preparatory rite as before — a lakh for each letter, living on milk — and offer red lotuses soaked in the three sweets.
A man whose mantra is perfected by japa, libation, oblation, worship and sprinkling should perform the applications described; otherwise the deities of that mantra,
angered, devour his life at that very moment, O sage. There is nothing in the world that cannot be accomplished by this vidya.
At the foot of a banyan in the forest, in caves on mountain tops, in the midst of gardens and wildernesses, at the foot of the Mothers' tree,
on the seashore and in the forest a man should propitiate these yakshinis. With lotuses, water-lilies red and white, and fragrant blue lotuses,
with fragrant shephalika smeared with the three sweets, as prescribed, by oblation on seven weekdays, within that mandala,
one gains victory in battle, in duels, in wrestling, in armed combat, in debate and in gambling,
and surely gains victory in all dealings. By oblation of chaturangula flowers one paralyses enemies,
and likewise with karnikara, punnaga, nameru, champaka, ketaka, rajavriksha and madhavi flowers;
offering these seven flowers in turn on the weekdays as before, the paralysis or defeat of the enemy surely comes about.
By offering the fuel of the enemy's constellation-tree into a fire of the same, soaked in mustard and ghee, the enemies bow at one's feet.
In a fire of death-wood one should duly offer the leaves, flowers, fruits and fuel of the death-tree on that weekday, preceded by worship;
the enemy's fourfold army is afflicted by disease, and thereby victory comes, or even the enemy's death.
On Sunday, in a fire kindled with arka fuel, one should offer in order its leaves, flowers, fruits, stems and roots,
soaked in the ghee of a red cow with a calf of the same colour, for a mandala, facing the enemy's direction, in a triangular pit as prescribed;
the enemy flees or, stricken with disease and fear, bows down. In a fire of palasha fuel, with its five parts soaked in that ghee,
by oblation on Monday it comes about as before without doubt; in a fire of khadira fuel with its five parts soaked in that ghee,
by oblation on Tuesday one surely obtains it; with apamarga on Wednesday, pippala on Thursday,
udumbara on Friday and shami on Saturday, with cow ghee, and with white, yellow, pale and dark colours as before,
one obtains that fruit in a fire kindled with those fuels. Beginning from the first lunar day up to the fifth in order,
by oblation of rice, chickpeas, mung, barley and black gram soaked in buffalo ghee, one obtains it on those days;
from the sixth to the seventh with goat ghee and husked grains as described before, one obtains the fruit described before;
in the following five with all these and the two kinds of sesame, with white rice, milk-rice soaked in sheep's ghee,
by oblation one obtains the fruit stated at first. So too in a fire from the constellation-tree, with these soaked in honey,
by oblation it is surely attained, without doubt. Having first perfected the vidya, the wise one should then perform all the applications described,
by the grace of Mangala. Having worshipped the deity, [taking] a brahmin girl or a maiden,
with auspicious limbs, innocent, bathed, in clean garments, auspicious, or a boy of the same kind, seating and worshipping them with the vidya,
touching the head, one should recite the vidya a hundred times and worship with red or white fragrant flowers,
and offer guggulu incense until the rite ends. Then, when the Goddess has entered that child, worshipping with devotion,
the vow-keeper, worshipping her with the offerings described and reciting the vidya, should ask what he wishes, and she will tell —
past, present and future, and whatever else is in the mind, and past births; worshipped, she will tell everything.
Then, worshipping her as before and dismissing her into oneself, one should recite it a thousand times; steady-minded and fulfilled, one lives happily.
By oblation for a mandala with red lotuses sprinkled with the three sweets one gains prosperity, and with white ones great fame.
By oblation of red lotuses smeared with honey over the stated period one gains gold, treasure or land.
By oblation of water-lilies smeared with milk one gains the desire stated; quickly various grains, and that man becomes fortunate.
By oblation of blue lotuses smeared with ghee one gains what one desires; with kahlara smeared with the same one becomes dear to the king.
By oblation of palasha flowers joined with the three sweets over that period, fourfold learning surely comes, without doubt.
By oblation of parched rice with the three sweets over that period, one gains a maiden as wife endowed with every virtue.
Offering coconut pulp with sugar or jaggery, smeared with honey, one becomes effortlessly like Kubera.
Likewise by oblation of food and ghee, or rice and sesame, or red flowers, or bandhuka flowers,
and with white flowers, one gains success in speech; with white and red mixed, one gains long life and health.
By oblation of triple durva sprigs smeared with the three sweets one conquers them; likewise by oblation of guduchi, milk-rice and sesame,
and hundred-petalled lotuses mixed with sandal paste and camphor, one gains prosperity that lasts through one's line.
Grinding saffron with cool water, mixed with camphor, and offering fully blown kahlara flowers rubbed with that paste,
one becomes like a king in prosperity and lives a hundred years on earth, without rivals, without fear, beyond the pairs, pure in heart.
By oblation of pieces of sugarcane one gains garments; likewise with red and white oleander flowers.
By oblation of patala flowers smeared with honey one brings women under control; likewise by oblation of lotuses one brings a courtesan under control.
By oblation of white things soaked in the milk of a white cow with a calf of like form, even a most sinful-minded man gains incomparable prosperity.
By oblation of cotton seeds smeared with sour gruel over that period, in a half-moon pit, enemies surely come under control, O sage.
By oblation of arishta leaves and seeds in its fire, and of death-seeds sprinkled with neem oil, one kills them.
Diseased horses likewise [are cured] by oblation of the five cow products, surely; oblation of aksha seeds smeared with oil destroys all.
By oblation of karanja seeds sprinkled [with oil] the enemy becomes possessed by pishachas; likewise by oblation of the five parts of the aksha tree.
By oblation of aksha seeds with neem oil, on that day the enemy surely becomes epileptic.
In a fire of fuel from the tree of the enemy's birth-constellation, by oblation of the flesh of his birth-animal, one brings death to the enemy.
By oblation of lotus seeds smeared with mustard oil, leprous diseases arise in the enemies that destroy the body.
By oblation of pepper and mustard smeared with oil at midnight, the enemy is surely seized that very day by burning fever.
In such rites of restraint, for one's own protection daily one should have japa, oblation and the like performed by friends who have gained the true vidya,
either with the Mrityunjaya mantra or with the vidyas belonging to those applications; otherwise the perfected mantra quickly destroys him.
Three lakhs are prescribed in the Krita age, double that in the Treta, triple in the Dvapara, and fourfold in the Kali.
The oblation should be a tenth, the libation a tenth of that, the sprinkling a tenth of that, and the feeding of brahmins a tenth of that.
In this order, whatever number of japa belongs to each of them should be done for the perfection of the vidya; then one should perform the applications.
For Kameshvari the japa should be double, O lord of sages; when the mantra is perfected one should perform the applications as appropriate.
For Bhagamala the japa is declared to be a lakh, and the oblation and the rest a tenth of that, for the perfection of the vidya, O lord of sages.
For Nityaklinna the japa is declared a lakh and the oblation a tenth, for perfection of the vidya; then one should perform the applications.
Then, silent and living on milk, one should recite nine lakhs; the Bherunda mantra has been described; the rest should be done with care.
For Vahnivasini three lakhs of japa are declared; all else should be done as before by the best practitioners.
For the vidya of Mahavajreshvari three lakhs of japa are held; the oblation and the rest should be a tenth, in the order described.
Untiring, one should recite the Duti mantra a lakh times, O sage, with the oblation and the rest a tenth in the prescribed way.
One should recite Tvarita a lakh times and perform all the oblations and the rest at a tenth, for the perfection of the vidya, O lord of sages.
For the vidya of Kulasundari the japa is declared a lakh, and the oblation and the rest a tenth, O best of brahmins.
For Nityanitya the japa is held to be three lakhs, O brahmin, with the oblation and the rest a tenth, by the stated procedure.
Fifty-three lakhs of japa are declared, with discipline, O lord of sages, for Nityapataka, and the oblation and the rest a tenth.
For Vijaya the japa is declared as one lakh, O Narada; the other means for perfecting the vidya are as described before.
One should recite Sarvamangalika thirty-two lakh times, and the oblation and the rest are declared at a tenth.
Eating only sacrificial food, one should recite Jvalamalinika eight lakh times, with the oblation and the rest a tenth, with the substances stated.
For Chitra the japa is sixteen lakhs, then the oblation and the rest; they should be done by the stated procedure for the perfection of the vidya, O lord of sages.
Thus the chapter on the Nityas has been told in brief from the beginning; all of it should be understood here together with the practice of the yantras.
Kshudha is the seventh, and Trisha is declared the eighth, from the Rudra forms; these begin with Om and are joined with 'namah.'
On the private parts, the two thighs, the knees, shanks and buttocks, the hip and the two sides, one should place the thirteen Vama digits.
The first digit is Ruja, with 'vamadevaya namah' at the end; with 'jyeshthaya namah' the second is declared, Raksha;
Kalakama is the fifth, then with 'vikaranaya namah' Samyamani is declared the sixth next;
Balakriya is the seventh digit, with 'vikaranaya'; with 'namah' Vriddhi is the eighth; and after 'bala,' the digit Sthira;
then with 'pramathanaya namah' Ratri is declared; with 'sarvabhutadamanaya namah' the digit Bhramani;
with 'namah' Mohini is declared by knowers of mantras as the twelfth digit; then with 'manonmanyai namah' Jvara is declared the thirteenth.
They are declared beginning with the pranava, in the dative, ending with 'namah.' One should place them on the feet, arms, breasts, nose, head and both arms.
The eight mantras born of Sadyojata are the digits in order: 'sadyojatam prapadyami' — Siddhi is the first digit;
again 'sadyojataya vai namah' — Vriddhi is declared; Dyuti is the third; then 'abhave,'
Lakshmi is declared the fourth; then the words 'nati bhave,' Medha is declared the fifth digit; again 'bhavasva mam,'
Prajna is declared the sixth; at the end of 'bhava,' the digit Prabha; then 'udbhavaya namah,' Sudha is the eighth digit.
All the digits begin with the pranava, are in the dative and joined with 'namah'; thirty-eight digits are declared, beginning with the five Brahma-mantras.
With his body thus placed, he becomes Gangadhara himself; then, concentrated, he should meditate thus on Sadashiva:
with five faces coloured white, yellow, dark, pale and like the hibiscus, with eyes, crowned with the moon, radiant as a crore of full moons,
holding in his hands trident, chisel, sword, thunderbolt, fire and the lord of serpents, shining with ornaments, and bell, noose, boon and fearlessness.
Meditating thus, one should recite the mantra five lakh times and offer a tenth of that with oleander flowers soaked in honey.
One should worship on the pedestal described before, form the image with the root mantra, invoke him and worship him in that image with the enclosures:
Ishana, holding spear, damaru, fearlessness and boon, three-eyed and white, one should worship in the north-east;
Tatpurusha, holding axe, deer, boon and fearlessness, bright as lightning, four-faced and three-eyed, one should worship in the east;
holding rosary, Veda and noose, rishti and damaru, khatvanga, sharp trident and skull in his hands,
black as collyrium, four-faced, with terrible teeth and fearsome — Aghora, three-eyed, the best knower of mantras should worship in the south;
Vamadeva, saffron-coloured, four-faced, three-eyed, holding deer, rosary, fearlessness and boon in his hands, four-faced,
his crown shining with the crescent moon, one should worship in the west; Sadyojata, like camphor and the moon, gentle, three-eyed,
holding boon, fearlessness, rosary and axe in his hands, graceful, with smiling face, one should worship properly in the north.
In the corners one should worship in order the radiant digits beginning with Nivritti, and on the petals all around Vighneshvara, Ananta and the others;
then outside Uma and the others, and Shakra and the others with their weapons. Having thus worshipped the Lord of gods with supreme devotion,
one should please him with dances, songs and the like, and with charming hymns. Tara, Maya, Viyat, bindu, Manu and a vowel,
joined with the five-syllable mantra — this is held to be the eight-syllable mantra; the wise should perform the limb-placements and the rest as for the five-syllable one.
[Meditate on] Shiva, lord of all, vermilion in colour, with a shining jewelled crown and the moon on his head, with divine ornaments and unguents, with a serpent as sacred thread,
his hand placed on the breast of his beloved seated on his left thigh, holding Veda, chisel, deer and fearlessness.
One should recite the mantra eight lakh times and offer a thousand oblations of milk-rice with ghee; on the pedestal one should form the image with the root mantra.
The enclosures: first the limbs, then Ananta and the others, the third declared with Uma and the others, and the world-lords,
and the fourth and fifth declared with their weapons. Thus the best practitioner should worship the god daily,
and obtaining prosperity reaching to sons and grandsons, he rejoices here. Tara, Sthira with the ear and moon, Bhrigu with visarga —
this is declared the three-syllable mantra of Mrityunjaya; its seer is Kahola, its metre Devi-Gayatri,
and its deity is declared to be Mahadeva Mrityunjaya; one should perform the six limbs with Bhrigu joined with the long vowels.
With eyes of moon, sun and fire, smiling, seated on a pair of lotuses, his hands shining with mudra, noose, deer and rosary, radiant as the moon,
his body adorned and drenched with nectar flowing from the moon on his forehead, with necklaces and the rest — one should meditate on him, who enchants the universe by his radiance.
The wise should recite the mantra three lakh times and offer a tenth of that with pieces of guduchi soaked in pure milk and ghee.
One should worship on the Shaiva pedestal, forming the image with the root mantra; having worshipped the enclosure of limbs, one should then worship the world-lords,
and then outside their weapons, the best practitioner should worship. When this mantra is perfected by japa, worship and the like, O best of sages,
one should perform the applications stated in the kalpa for the fruits desired. Offering daily with reverence pieces of guduchi sprinkled with milk,
a thousand for a month, one gains long life, wealth and sons. Guduchi, banyan ..., milk, ghee, milk and havis —
seven substances on the seven weekdays in order, a thousand of each; one should daily feed more than seven brahmins with sweet food,
give the priests a fee of a red milch cow, and then please the teacher with wealth and the like, regarding him as the deity.
By this procedure the target, freed from black magic, treachery, fever and the like, lives long and easily for a hundred years.
In sorcery, fever, paralysis, terrible madness, head disease, incurable disease, affliction by poison, delusion, burning and great fear,
this oblation is declared to bring peace and grant freedom from all fear; one should offer these substances duly on the three birth-days,
and feed brahmins who have mastered the Veda with sweet foods; one gains long life and obtains the prosperity one desires.
The wise should offer eleven oblations of durva daily; one then conquers untimely death, and long life and health increase.
An oblation made on the three birth-days with excellent fuel of guduchi, kashmiri and bakula removes all death and disease.
An oblation made with white mustard destroys great fever; an oblation of apamarga fuel removes all illnesses.
First 'dakshinamurtaye,' then the word 'tubhyam,' then at the end of 'vatamula' one should say 'nivasine,'
'dhyanaika-niratangaya,' then the word 'namah,' 'rudraya shambhave,' enclosed with Tara and Shakti — this is declared
the thirty-six-syllable mantra that grants the fruit of all desires; its seer is declared to be Shuka and its metre Anushtubh,
and its deity Dakshinamurti, named Shambhu. With mantra-syllables joined first with Tara and Shakti, beginning and ending with Hrim,
with the fire-letters in groups of six, six and eight, the limbs beginning with the heart are formed. On the head, forehead, eyes, ears, both cheeks and nose,
mouth, arm-joints, neck, breasts, heart, navel, hip, private parts and again the foot-joints one should place the letters of the mantra,
and then perform the pervading placement on the body with Tara and Shakti. On a lovely slope of the Himalaya, frequented by Siddhas and Kinnaras,
shaded on all sides from the sun by the branches of various trees, with flowering trees embraced by nets of blossoming creepers,
cool with breezes from waterfalls issuing from rock clefts, with troops of celestial women singing and flocks of peacocks dancing,
the directions made vocal by flocks of cooing cuckoos, frequented by animals who have given up their mutual enmity,
adorned with fragrant flowers of water and land, ever enjoyed by the first sages beginning with Shuka,
watched by the gods led by Purandara with their consorts — [there is] a very tall banyan tree, shining with ruby fruits,
beautiful with dense leaves of emerald, adorned with hanging ornaments of the nine gems,
a wonder whose shade is skilled in cutting off the heat of worldly existence. At its root, on an auspicious, well-fashioned jewelled throne,
[one should remember Hara] seated, adorned in black, with a face like the autumn moon, like Mount Kailasa, three-eyed, his matted locks marked with the moon,
intent on gazing at the tip of his nose, seated in the hero's posture, his tender hand resting on his knee rich with deerskin on the bhadra seat,
with a serpent bound at his armpit, most gracious — so should one remember Hara. One should recite the mantra three lakh and twenty thousand times,
and offer a tenth of that with pure sesame mixed with milk; one should worship him on the pedestal described for the five-syllable mantra, by that procedure.
Living on alms, with senses conquered, one should recite this mantra for a month, four thousand times daily, and gains supreme glory of speech.
One should drink milk consecrated three times with this mantra; by meditation on Dakshinamurti one becomes an expounder of the scriptures.
The pranava, the heart syllable, then the word 'bhagavate,' 'dakshinamurtaye' in the dative, then 'mahyam medham,'
'prayachchha' ending with two 'tha's — this is the twenty-two-syllable mantra; its seer is the four-faced one, its metre Gayatri, and its deity as stated.
With the six long vowels enclosed by Tara one should form the limbs, or with the words of the mantra; the meditation and the rest are as before.
The red one with a high seat, Sadya with the bindu is first; then the second, abiding in the fire seed, long, adorned with Shanti and the moon;
the third, the letter of Langalisha — the mantra with three seeds is declared to be of the nature of Nilakantha, supremely removing both kinds of poison.
'Hara' twice and the wife of Fire is declared the heart mantra; 'kapardine' twice is declared the head mantra;
'nilakanthaya' with two 'tha's is declared the topknot mantra; at the end of the word 'kalakuta,' 'vishabhakshana' in the dative,
'hum phat' is declared the armour; 'nilakanthine' ending with 'svaha' is the weapon — these they know as the five limbs of the mantra.
On the head, throat and heart-lotus one should place the three seeds in order. [Meditate on] Hara, radiant as ten thousand rising suns, shining with matted locks and the moon,
adorned with serpents, holding a rosary, trident, Brahma's skull and khatvanga in his arms, three-eyed.
One should recite the mantra three lakh times and offer a tenth of that with havis and ghee duly into a consecrated fire.
One should worship the god Nilakantha with concentration on the Shaiva pedestal, by the procedure of Mrityunjaya; it destroys both kinds of poison.
Agni, Samvartaka, Aditya, Ra and Anila with the sixtieth and bindu — the seed famed as Chintamani, granting all prosperity.
Its seer is declared to be Kashyapa, its metre Anushtubh, and its deity Ardhanarishvara, lord of the worlds.
With the six consonants beginning with ra one should make the six limbs in order. [Meditate on him] three-eyed, like a blue gem, holding trident, noose, skull
and a red lotus in his lotus hands, with lovely ornaments, his crown bound with the crescent moon — so remember Ardhanarishvara.
One should recite the mantra one lakh times and offer three hundred oblations of sesame soaked in sweets; one should worship on the Shaiva pedestal with the enclosures of the limbs,
then with Vrisha and the others, the Mothers, the world-guardians and their weapons. One should recite the Prasada mantra ten thousand times for the quelling of disease.
This seed encircled by 'svaha,' dripping supreme nectar, meditated on in the orb of the moon on the head, removes poison and disease.
The seed rich in vowels in reverse order, placed in the house of fire, surrounded outside by a hexagon shining with the consonants beginning with ra —
remembered on the head of one possessed by a spirit, it quickly destroys the spirit; remembered on an afflicted limb, it surely quells that affliction.
The pranava, the heart syllable, then 'pashupataye' in the dative, again Tara, 'namah,' the word 'bhuta,' then 'adhipataye' —
'namo rudraya' twice, from the words 'khadga-ravana,' 'vihara' twice, then 'nari nritya' twice separately,
after 'shmashana-bhasmachita,' then 'sharanyaya,' again the word 'ghanta-kapala-maladi-dharaya,'
after the word 'vyaghracharma,' 'paridhanaya,' after 'shashanka-krita,' 'shekharaya,'
after 'krishnasarpa,' one should say 'yajnopavitine,' 'bala' twice, 'chala' twice, 'anivartakapaline,'
'hanu' twice, then 'bhutan trasaya' twice, again 'mandalamadhye,' then 'kata' twice,
'rudrankushena shamaya,' 'praveshaya' twice, then 'aveshaya' twice, and then say the word 'chandasi' —
'dharadhipati-rudro 'yam jnapayati,' and the beautiful one of Fire — this Khadgaravana mantra has one hundred and seventy syllables.
'Bhutadhipataye svaha' is declared the worship mantra; this perfected mantra becomes effective by japa alone;
after twenty thousand recitations one becomes able to seize spirits and the like. Maya, 'sphura' twice, again 'prasphura' twice,
'ghataya' twice, ending with the armour syllable and 'phat' — this great fifty-one-syllable mantra is the Aghora weapon.
Its seer is declared to be Aghora, its metre Trivrit, and its deity, the lord of the mantra, Aghora-Rudra.
The heart is declared with five, the head with six, the topknot with ten, the armour with nine,
the eye with eight letters, and the weapon with ten. On the head, eyes, mouth, throat, heart, navel and thighs in order,
and on the knees, shanks and feet, one should place the letters divided by eleven — with five, six, eight, four, six, two, two, four, six and two.
One should meditate on Sadashiva called Aghora: dark, three-eyed, with serpents, with red garments and unguents, holding many weapons.
This mantra destroys ghosts, vetalas and the like in restraining them. Tara, the one ending in va on Dhara, adorned with the left eye and the moon,
Pashi, Baka, the ear and eye, ending with the armour and weapon syllables — the six-syllable mantra called Pashupatastra, warding off planets and petty spirits.
With the six letters one makes the six limbs, ending with 'hum phat' with the jatis. One should remember Hara Pashupati, radiant as the midday sun, terrible, three-eyed, adorned with serpents,
with many weapons and four faces. One should recite the mantra a lakh times for each letter and offer a tenth of that
with cow's ghee into a consecrated fire; one should worship on the Shaiva pedestal with the limbs, Mothers, world-lords and weapons.
Water consecrated with this should be thrown into the mouth of one possessed; at once the spirit leaves, crying out, by the power of the great mantra.
The man who shoots arrows consecrated with this in battle conquers all his enemies in a moment, like a second Partha.
The last letter with the bindu, 'kshetrapalaya' and the heart syllable —
beginning with Tara, this is the eight-syllable mantra of Kshetrapala; placing the six limbs with the seed joined with the six long vowels, one should meditate:
like a blue mountain, clothed by the directions, adorned with serpents, three-eyed, with tawny hair standing up, holding a skull and a mace — so remember him.
One should recite the mantra one lakh times and offer a tenth of that with charu sprinkled with ghee; then worship him in the field
on a pedestal formed of Dharma and the rest, with his limbs and enclosures, with reverence; and offer a bali to him and his retinue with this:
first 'ehi' twice, then 'vidvisham purusham' twice, 'bhanjaya' twice, again 'nartaya' twice,
then 'vighna' twice, 'mahabhairava,' then 'kshetrapala-balim grihna' twice, and the beautiful one of Fire —
this bali mantra is declared, granting the fruit of all desires. Making a large ball with instruction, the practitioner at night,
remembering the lord of the field as described, should place the bali in his hand; pleased by this bali, Kshetrapala grants
beauty, intelligence, strength, health, radiance, nourishment, fame and prosperity. One should extract 'batukaya' in the dative and 'apaduddharanaya' likewise,
'kuru' twice, then again say 'batukaya' in the dative; enclosed with Shakti and beginning with Dhruva — this is the twenty-two-syllable mantra.
The limbs of the mantra are made with two, four, seven, four, four and one letters. [Meditate on] the child, like crystal, his face shining and playful,
his body radiant with divine ornaments, three-eyed, holding staff and trident, most gracious, removing the fear of devotees — so remember him with devotion.
Eating only sacrificial food, with senses conquered, one should recite the mantra a lakh times for each letter, and offer a tenth of that with sesame joined with sweets.
On a pedestal formed of Dharma and the rest, on a very beautiful lotus, with a sky-lotus within a triangle inside a hexagon,
one should worship the god Batuka with his limbs and enclosures in order. "Drink the blood and eat the flesh of the enemy's side day by day, together with your hosts and your dogs" —
this bali mantra is declared, interwoven with the enemy's name; pleased by this bali, Batuka, angered,
cuts up the enemy army and divides the flesh among his hosts. Ankusha, Vahnishikhara, ending with la and da — so it is declared;
ending with 'phat,' this three-lettered mantra of Chanda is declared; its seer is Trita and its metre Anushtubh;
its deity is Chandesha; the forming of the limbs will be told: the heart is 'dipta phat,' the head 'jvala phat,'
the topknot 'jvalini phat,' the armour 'vaha phat,' the eye 'hala phat,' and 'sarvajvalini phat' next.
Placing the six limbs thus, one should then meditate on the god Chandeshvara, red-bodied, three-eyed, clad in red,
holding trident, rosary, chisel and water-pot. One should recite the mantra a lakh times for each letter and perform the oblation at a tenth
with pure sesame and rice joined with the three sweets; on the pedestal described for the five-syllable mantra one should form the image with the root mantra.
Kurmesha with the bindu, then 'chandeshvaraya' and the heart syllable — this mantra is declared for the worship of Chandesha.
The enclosure is with the limbs, the Mothers, the lords of the directions and the thunderbolt and other weapons. One skilled in Shaiva mantras should recite the mantra of Chandeshvara;
he obtains all desires and rejoices here and hereafter. Hear, Narada, I will tell the divine hymn to Maheshvara,
by whose recitation in worship all mantras are perfected.
To Shankara, whose forms are earth, water, fire, wind, space, the sacrificer, the moon and the sun, who dwells within all beings, salutations again and again.
To him who dwells at the end of the Veda, who is the Veda and the source of the Veda, to the radiance beyond the senses, to the eternal one, salutations again and again.
To Shambhu, who cannot be indicated by the division of gross and subtle, to Bhava, destroyer of the sorrow born of existence, salutations again and again.
To him who is far beyond the path of reasoning, who grants the fruit of austerities, generous with the four aims of life, to the all-knowing one, salutations again and again.
To him who has no beginning, middle or end, who has removed all fear, the great one to be meditated on by yogis, to the one beyond qualities, salutations again and again.
To the Self of the universe, the solitary one, whose head is adorned with the shining moon, destroyer of Kandarpa's pride, slayer of Time, salutations again and again.
To him who swallowed poison, who rides on the shoulder of the playful bull, whose matted locks are bound with the garland of the river, salutations again and again.
To the pure one, pure in nature, the inner Self of the pure, destroyer of the cities, the full one, of holy name, salutations again and again.
To him who is devoted to his own devotees and grants them enjoyment and liberation, to the unclothed one, the abode, the lord of all, salutations.
To the root of the three forms, the three-eyed, the trident-bearer, whose abode is threefold, whose form is light, the giver of birth, salutations again and again.
